# Landowner visit etiquette

Every AWS station except AWS-01 sits on private land under a verbal or
written agreement with the landowner. The equipment is ours; the ground is
not. These rules exist because one bad visit can end a relationship that
took months to build, and without landowners there is no network.

## Before you arrive

Check the access notes for the site you are visiting. Some gates stay
unlocked on agreed days; others need a phone call the day before. Never
assume a new volunteer knows the arrangement — pass the landowner's
preferred contact method explicitly when handing over a round. If the
visit involves climbing or stays longer than an hour, the fieldwork safety
check-in rules apply as well.

Park in the agreed place. At AWS-03 that is the lay-by on the lane, not the
farmyard. At AWS-08 it is the field entrance, not across the crop edge.
Tyre tracks in soft ground show up for weeks and are the fastest way to get
a complaint.

## On site behaviour

Close gates behind you every time, even if you found them open. Dogs and
livestock take priority over finishing a voltage check; wait or come back.
Do not bring visitors who are not part of the maintenance rota without
asking the landowner first. One extra person at AWS-05 in November 2025
was fine because we asked; showing up with a photographer would not have
been.

Keep noise and litter to zero. Pack out everything you packed in, including
stripped cable ties and glove wrappers. If you need to move a temporary
obstacle to reach the enclosure, put it back exactly where it was.

## When something goes wrong

If you break a fence wire, strand of wire, or anything else that is not
our equipment, report it to the landowner the same day and tell the group
coordinator. Do not leave a note in the letterbox and consider it done.
If the landowner is unhappy about access times, noise, or vehicle use,
stop the visit, apologise, and escalate to whoever signed the original
agreement.

## Ending the relationship

If we decommission a site, we remove the mast, fill the footing hole, and
restore the ground as best we can. The landowner gets a copy of the final
readings archive if they want it. Access permission is not transferable:
if land changes hands, the new owner must agree before anyone visits again.
